King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Then fled Queen Guinevere to Amesbury to a nunnery, and there she

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: clothed herself in sackcloth, and spent her time in praying for the king

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: and in good deeds and fasting. And in that nunnery evermore she lived,

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: sorely repenting and mourning for her sin, and for the ruin she had

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: brought on all the realm. And there anon she died.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: And when Sir Lancelot heard thereof, he put his knightly armor off, and

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: bade farewell to all his kin, and went a mighty pilgrimage for many

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: years, and after lived a hermit till his death.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: When Sir Modred came to Dover, he found King Arthur and his army but

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: just landed; and there they fought a fierce and bloody battle, and many

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: great and noble knights fell on both sides.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: But the king's side had the victory, for he was beyond himself with

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: might and passion, and all his knights so fiercely followed him, that,

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: in spite of all their multitude, they drove Sir Modred's army back with

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: fearful wounds and slaughter, and slept that night upon the

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: battle-field.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: But Sir Gawain was smitten by an arrow in the wound Sir Lancelot gave

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: him, and wounded to the death. Then was he borne to the king's tent,

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: and King Arthur sorrowed over him as it had been his own son. "Alas!"

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: said he; "in Sir Lancelot and in you I had my greatest earthly joy, and

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: now is all gone from me."

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: And Sir Gawain answered, with a feeble voice, "My lord and king, I know

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: well my death is come, and through my own wilfulness, for I am smitten

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: in the wound Sir Lancelot gave me. Alas! that I have been the cause of

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: all this war, for but for me thou hadst been now at peace with Lancelot,

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: and then had Modred never done this treason. I pray ye, therefore, my

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: dear lord, be now agreed with Lancelot, and tell him, that although he

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: gave me my death-wound, it was through my own seeking; wherefore I

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: beseech him to come back to England, and here to visit my tomb, and pray

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: for my soul."

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: When he had thus spoken, Sir Gawain gave up his ghost, and the king

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: grievously mourned for him.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Then they told him that the enemy had camped on Barham Downs, whereat,

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: with all his hosts, he straightway marched there, and fought again a

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: bloody battle, and overthrew Sir Modred utterly. Howbeit, he raised yet

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: another army, and retreating ever from before the king, increased his

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: numbers as he went, till at the farthest west in Lyonesse, he once more

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: made a stand.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Now, on the night of Trinity Sunday, being the eve of the battle, King

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Arthur had a vision, and saw Sir Gawain in a dream, who warned him not

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: to fight with Modred on the morrow, else he would be surely slain; and

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: prayed him to delay till Lancelot and his knights should come to aid

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: him.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: So when King Arthur woke he told his lords and knights that vision, and

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: all agreed to wait the coming of Sir Lancelot. Then a herald was sent

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: with a message of truce to Sir Modred, and a treaty was made that

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: neither army should assail the other.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: But when the treaty was agreed upon, and the heralds returned, King

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Arthur said to his knights, "Beware, lest Sir Modred deceive us, for I

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: in no wise trust him, and if swords be drawn be ready to encounter!" And

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Sir Modred likewise gave an order, that if any man of the king's army

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: drew his sword, they should begin to fight.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: And as it chanced, a knight of the king's side was bitten by an adder in

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: the foot, and hastily drew forth his sword to slay it. That saw Sir

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Modred, and forthwith commanded all his army to assail the king's.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: So both sides rushed to battle, and fought passing fiercely. And when

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: the king saw there was no hope to stay them, he did right mightily and

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: nobly as a king should do, and ever, like a lion, raged in the thickest

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: of the press, and slew on the right hand and on the left, till his horse

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: went fetlock deep in blood. So all day long they fought, and stinted not

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: till many a noble knight was slain.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: But the king was passing sorrowful to see his trusty knights lie dead on

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: every side. And at the last but two remained beside him, Sir Lucan, and

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: his brother, Sir Bedivere, and both were sorely wounded.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "Now am I come to mine end," said King Arthur; "but, lo! that traitor

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Modred liveth yet, and I may not die till I have slain him. Now, give me

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: my spear, Sir Lucan."

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "Lord, let him be," replied Sir Lucan; "for if ye pass through this

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: unhappy day, ye shall be right well revenged upon him. My good lord,

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: remember well your dream, and what the spirit of Sir Gawain did

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: fore-warn ye."

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "Betide me life, betide me death," said the king; "now I see him yonder

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: alone, he shall never escape my hands, for at a better vantage shall I

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: never have him."

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "God speed you well," said Sir Bedivere.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Then King Arthur got his spear in both his hands, and ran towards Sir

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Modred, crying, "Traitor, now is thy death-day come!" And when Sir

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Modred heard his words, and saw him come, he drew his sword and stood to

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: meet him. Then King Arthur smote Sir Modred through the body more than a

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: fathom. And when Sir Modred felt he had his death wound, he thrust

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: himself with all his might up to the end of King Arthur's spear, and

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: smote his father, Arthur, with his sword upon the head, so that it

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: pierced both helm and brain-pan.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: And therewith Sir Modred fell down stark dead to the earth, and King

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Arthur fell down also in a swoon, and swooned many times.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Then Sir Lucan and Sir Bedivere came and bare him away to a little

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: chapel by the sea-shore. And there Sir Lucan sank down with the

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: bleeding of his own wounds, and fell dead.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: And King Arthur lay long in a swoon, and when he came to himself, he

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: found Sir Lucan lying dead beside him, and Sir Bedivere weeping over the

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: body of his brother.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Then said the king to Sir Bedivere, "Weeping will avail no longer, else

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: would I grieve forevermore. Alas! now is the fellowship of the Round

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Table dissolved forever, and all my realm I have so loved is wasted with

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: war. But my time hieth fast, wherefore take thou Excalibur, my good

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: sword, and go therewith to yonder water-side and throw it in, and bring

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: me word what thing thou seest."

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: So Sir Bedivere departed; but as he went he looked upon the sword, the

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: hilt whereof was all inlaid with precious stones exceeding rich. And

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: presently he said within himself, "If I now throw this sword into the

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: water, what good should come of it?" So he hid the sword among the

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: reeds, and came again to the king.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "What sawest thou?" said he to Sir Bedivere.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "Lord," said he, "I saw nothing else but wind and waves."

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "Thou hast untruly spoken," said the king; "wherefore go lightly back

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: and throw it in, and spare not."

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Then Sir Bedivere returned again, and took the sword up in his hand; but

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: when he looked on it, he thought it sin and shame to throw away a thing

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: so noble. Wherefore he hid it yet again, and went back to the king.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "What saw ye?" said King Arthur.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "Lord," answered he, "I saw nothing but the water ebbing and flowing."

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "Oh, traitor and untrue!" cried out the king; "twice hast thou now

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: betrayed me. Art thou called of men a noble knight, and wouldest betray

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: me for a jewelled sword? Now, therefore, go again for the last time, for

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: thy tarrying hath put me in sore peril of my life, and I fear my wound

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: hath taken cold; and if thou do it not this time, by my faith I will

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: arise and slay thee with my hands."

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Then Sir Bedivere ran quickly and took up the sword, and went down to

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: the water's edge, and bound the girdle round the hilt and threw it far

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: into the water. And lo! an arm and hand came forth above the water, and

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: caught the sword, and brandished it three times, and vanished.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: So Sir Bedivere came again to the king and told him what he had seen.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "Help me from hence," said King Arthur; "for I dread me I have tarried

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: over long."

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Then Sir Bedivere took the king up in his arms, and bore him to the

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: water's edge. And by the shore they saw a barge with three fair queens

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: therein, all dressed in black, and when they saw King Arthur they wept

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: and wailed.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "Now put me in the barge," said he to Sir Bedivere, and tenderly he did

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: so.

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Then the three queens received him, and he laid his head upon the lap of

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: one of them, who cried, "Alas! dear brother, why have ye tarried so

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: long, for your wound hath taken cold?"

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: With that the barge put from the land, and when Sir Bedivere saw it

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: departing, he cried with a bitter cry, "Alas! my lord King Arthur, what

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: shall become of me now ye have gone from me?"

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: "Comfort ye," said King Arthur, "and be strong, for I may no more help

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: ye. I go to the Vale of Avilion to heal me of my grievous wound, and if

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: ye see me no more, pray for my soul."

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Then the three queens kneeled down around the king and sorely wept and

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: wailed, and the barge went forth to sea, and departed slowly out of Sir

title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
text: Bedivere's sight.

King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
